sentence: The course aims to develop students' ability to understand, design and implement programmes in C language, applying structured programming principles.
rationale: Designing and implementing structured C programs is general computer programming. ESCO has no skill for the C language itself (it has C#, C++, Objective-C).

sentence: The aim is for students to become autonomous in the use of Unix/Linux environments, master the process of compilation and execution via command line, and understand the complete software development cycle.
rationale: Unix/Linux use and command-line work -> operating systems. 'Complete software development cycle' -> systems development life-cycle. No ESCO skill names Unix shell use or command-line compilation.

sentence: By the end of the course, students should be able to analyse problems, break down solutions into functions and modules, use control structures, arrays, pointers, strings and data structures appropriately, and manipulate files and dynamic memory.
rationale: Control structures, arrays, pointers, files and dynamic memory are core programming. Breaking problems down into functions and modules matches task algorithmisation.

sentence: The course also aims to foster good practices in organisation, documentation and code testing, promoting the rigour and clarity essential to engineering programming.
rationale: Good practice, organisation and rigour -> implement ICT coding conventions. Code testing -> execute software tests. Documentation is mentioned only in passing; 'provide technical documentation' is about production documents, so I left it out.

sentence: The C Programming course introduces the fundamentals of structured programming, integrating the use of Unix/Linux systems and command line compilation.
rationale: An introduction to structured programming -> computer programming. Unix/Linux and command-line compilation -> operating systems.

sentence: The essential concepts of the C language are covered: programme structure, data types, operators and flow control.
rationale: Language basics (program structure, types, operators, flow control) are programming fundamentals. There is no C-specific ESCO skill.

sentence: Skills are developed in modularisation with functions, use of arrays, pointers, strings and structures (struct).
rationale: Functions, arrays, pointers, strings and structs are programming constructs, covered by computer programming.

sentence: It also includes working with text and binary files, command line arguments and dynamic memory, culminating in the organisation of programmes in multiple files using make.
rationale: File I/O, command-line arguments, dynamic memory and multi-file builds are programming topics. No ESCO skill covers make or build tools; 'tools for software configuration management' (Puppet, Chef and similar) is a different thing.

sentence: The course aims to provide students with a solid foundation for understanding, developing and testing small and medium complexity programmes in C, applying good practices of readability and efficiency.
rationale: Developing programs -> computer programming. Testing -> execute software tests. Good practice in readability and efficiency -> implement ICT coding conventions.

sentence: Develop algorithms for the solution of specific problems
rationale: Developing algorithms for given problems matches algorithms and task algorithmisation.

sentence: Implement programs and scripts using a programming language
rationale: 'Programs' -> computer programming. 'Scripts' -> use scripting programming.

sentence: Do debugging of computer programs
rationale: Debugging programs is the ESCO skill debug software.

sentence: The teaching methodology associated with the curricular unit will be based on a problem-based learning approach, with theoretical-practical classes involving the exposure of different programmatic concepts, and the autonomous resolution of practical problems for consolidation of knowledge.
rationale: No skill: this describes the teaching method (problem-based learning), not something students learn. 'apply teaching strategies' is a skill for teachers, not for students.

sentence: In the end, students should have skills in the domain of web technologies, allowing them to understand, intervene and collaborate in the web development process, so that it can be adapted for digital marketing, when used this means of communication.
rationale: Understanding and working in the web development process -> web programming. Digital marketing is named only as a use for these skills, not as something taught, so 'digital marketing techniques' is left out.

sentence: Web design main elements, using HTML
rationale: HTML -> use markup languages (its description names HTML). Web design elements -> implement front-end website design.

sentence: Web design customization, using CSS and Twitter Bootstrap
rationale: CSS -> CSS. Customizing a web design with CSS/Bootstrap -> implement front-end website design. ESCO has no Bootstrap skill.

sentence: JavaScript programming language
rationale: Direct match: JavaScript.

sentence: Programming DOM elements
rationale: DOM manipulation is done in JavaScript inside web pages -> JavaScript and web programming. ESCO has no DOM skill.

sentence: Information representation obtained in JSON.
rationale: ESCO has no JSON skill. 'information structure' (formats of structured and semi-structured data) is the closest knowledge concept for representing information in JSON. This is the weakest match in the set.

sentence: This micro-credential aims to equip students with a set of skills that are not only relevant but also indispensable in today's technology-driven scenario.
source_course: Microcredencial in Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) in C++
rationale: No skill: a generic promotional sentence that names no concrete skill or topic.

sentence: C++ is one of the most popular programming language in the world, due to the advantages it offers, such as high performance, object orientation, a high degree of flexibility, a wide variety of data structures and ready-to-use algorithms, among others.
source_course: Microcredencial in Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) in C++
rationale: Names C++ and object orientation; the course is about OOP in C++ -> C++ and use object-oriented programming.
